title: curl
definition: Client URL. A command-line tool for transferring data over various network protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, FTP). It is the industry standard for testing APIs from the terminal.
simpleExplanation: A web browser without a screen. You ask for a website, and instead of showing you pictures, it just dumps the raw HTML code onto your terminal.
realWorldExample: A developer is writing a REST API. To test it, they type `curl -X POST -d '{"user":"bob"}' http://localhost:3000/api/users`. The terminal prints out the JSON response from the server.

basic: Does `curl` process JavaScript or render images like Chrome does?
intermediate: What does the `-i` flag do in a `curl` command?

answers.question: Render JavaScript?
answers.answer: No. `curl` only fetches the raw text payload. It has no rendering engine.

answers.question: What is -i?
answers.answer: Include Headers. It forces `curl` to print the hidden HTTP headers (like Status Code 200 OK or 404 Not Found) before printing the actual webpage data.
